question: The rise in the number of charging stations for electric vehicles available for use in the EU has not been accompanied by uniform and transparent price display standards. Unlike users of traditional fuels, for which prices must be clearly displayed on fuel price boards visible from a distance, e-vehicle users have no physical signage to go on, and rates are often only accessible via digital applications or QR codes.

This lack of information and rate fragmentation creates uncertainty among consumers, leading to a significant imbalance that hampers the development of sustainable mobility and restricts free competition in the internal market. The absence of a requirement for prices to be displayed physically, as they are for traditional petrol pumps, raises serious transparency problems. In the light of the above: 1.
Will the Commission push for the introduction of a standardised obligation for operators to display prices, as is the case for fossil fuels?
Does it believe that the current fragmentation violates consumers’ rights to transparency?

What steps does it plan to take within the framework of the Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation to ensure that clearly comparable prices are available to customers before they use the charging stations?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.8.2026) Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 on the deployment of alternative fuels infrastructure1 sets clear rules on how operators of recharging points and mobility service providers must make price information available to consumers.

Article 5(4) of the Regulation requires that the operator of a publicly accessible recharging point with a power output at or above 50kW must show full price information on the ad hoc price and any possible occupancy fee at the recharging point. However, for recharging points below 50kW, this information must be made available, for example on an app, but its display at the recharging point is not required.

The Commission is currently reviewing Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 in accordance with Article 24 of the Regulation. This review addresses, among others, user aspects, including on price transparency issues. The Commission plans to adopt a legislative proposal for the amendment of the Regulation by the end of 2026.
1 Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 September 2023 on the
deployment of alternative fuels infrastructure, and repealing Directive 2014/94/EU, OJ L 234, 22.9.2023, pp. 1– 47.
